canonical.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not

parent.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

siblings.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
siblings.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

siblings.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose
siblings.summary: Office, Teams and mail are a tolerable compromise on Linux in 2026; OneDrive sync and OneNote are the two places where the gap is real.

siblings.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)
siblings.summary: Per-tool verdicts for the Windows-only utilities in an actual installed-software inventory: most transfer cleanly, AutoHotkey and Power Automate Desktop have no single answer, and Wayland is the variable that decides the rest.

siblings.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma 6.7 is the only Linux desktop that replaces most of DisplayFusion and FancyZones natively; Fences has no real equivalent and the X-Rite workflow becomes ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL plus a per-screen ICC profile.

siblings.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
siblings.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

siblings.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition
siblings.summary: Wine for single-window utilities, a local Windows VM for Visual Studio and SSMS, RDP for the corporate cluster — and no GPU passthrough on a muxless Legion.

sources.title: ProtonDB report summary — Age of Wonders: Planetfall (718850)
sources.claim: Age of Wonders: Planetfall sits at ProtonDB tier Gold with a Platinum trending tier and 95 reports as of 30 Jul 2026.

sources.title: Steam — Age of Wonders: Planetfall
sources.claim: Valve rates Age of Wonders: Planetfall as Playable (category 2) on Steam Deck, SteamOS and Steam Machine, with the default graphics config flagged performant and startup functional.

sources.title: GamingOnLinux — anti-cheat compatibility list
sources.claim: GamingOnLinux's anti-cheat compatibility list tracks 245 anti-cheat games: 146 Works, 92 Broken, 7 needing reports; Fall Guys records as Works.

sources.title: NVIDIA — Linux gaming driver documentation
sources.claim: NVIDIA's official Linux guidance replaces the NVIDIA App GUI with environment variables: PROTON_ENABLE_NGX_UPDATER, DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_*, NVPRESENT_ENABLE_SMOOTH_MOTION, DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX.

sources.title: Phoronix — Proton 11.0-1
sources.claim: Proton 11.0-1 shipped stable on 7 July 2026, rebased on Wine 11.0 with DXVK 2.7, VKD3D 1.19.

sources.title: ValveSoftware/Proton issue 2959 — Paradox Launcher 1603
sources.claim: The Proton bug for Age of Wonders: Planetfall — 'Failed to install Paradox Launcher: exit status 1603' — has been open since Aug 2019.

sources.title: Steam Community guide — Proton launcher bypass
sources.claim: Under Proton the usual '<path to exe> %command%' launcher bypass fails; the working pattern rewrites Proton's own command line with sed.

sources.title: Heroic Games Launcher
sources.claim: Heroic Games Launcher is a native client for the Epic, GOG and Amazon Prime libraries on Linux, Windows, macOS and Steam Deck.

sources.title: Heroic wiki — EOS Overlay
sources.claim: Heroic installs the Epic Online Services overlay once globally on Linux but requires enabling it per game, plus DXVK and the corefonts winetricks package.

sources.title: Heroic wiki — Fall Guys
sources.claim: Heroic's per-game wiki states Fall Guys works out of the box on Linux with the latest GE-Proton.

sources.title: AreWeAntiCheatYet — games dataset
sources.claim: The AreWeAntiCheatYet dataset lists Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout as status 'Running'; across 1166 games: 642 Broken, 276 Running, 194 Supported, 52 Denied.

sources.title: GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom (GE-Proton)
sources.claim: GE-Proton (proton-ge-custom) is the community Proton build that Heroic and most anti-cheat guides target.

sources.title: NVIDIA release notes 595.71.05 (Linux) / 596.36 (Windows)
sources.claim: NVIDIA ships Linux and Windows drivers as paired branches — release notes are titled 'Version 595.71.05(Linux)/596.36(Windows)'.

sources.title: Arch Linux news — NVIDIA 590 drops Pascal, switches to open kernel modules
sources.claim: From driver 590 NVIDIA dropped Pascal and older GPUs, and Turing and newer automatically move to the open kernel modules.

sources.title: flightlessmango/MangoHud
sources.claim: MangoHud is the Vulkan/OpenGL overlay for FPS, frame times, temperatures and CPU/GPU load on Linux — the FrameView/Game Bar overlay replacement.

sources.title: PhysX (Wikipedia)
sources.claim: PhysX is a cross-platform SDK that already targets Linux and has been open source under a 3-clause BSD licence since 3 Dec 2018.

sources.title: GamingOnLinux — NVIDIA 595.58.03 recommended stable
sources.claim: NVIDIA 595.58.03 became the recommended stable Linux driver on 24 Mar 2026; it fixes a kwin_wayland display-wake bug, kernel crashes on DisplayPort MST dock disconnect, and adds system-memory fallback.

sources.title: GPU Screen Recorder
sources.claim: GPU Screen Recorder is the direct ShadowPlay/Instant Replay replacement on Linux, using NVENC and keeping only the last few minutes.

sources.title: Xbox Support — Cloud Gaming supported browsers
sources.claim: Xbox Cloud Gaming in a browser is officially supported on Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome and Safari — both Edge and Chrome ship for Linux.

sources.title: GamingOnLinux — Discord screen sharing with audio on Wayland
sources.claim: Discord stable shipped full screen-sharing with audio on Linux/Wayland on 15 Jan 2025, but only for apps routed through PulseAudio, and it was absent from the Flathub build.

sources.title: Vencord/Vesktop
sources.claim: Vesktop is a third-party Discord desktop client whose headline feature is Linux screen-share with sound on Wayland.

sources.title: Epic Online Services — anti-cheat support for Linux, Mac and Steam Deck
sources.claim: Epic added Easy Anti-Cheat support for Linux, macOS and Steam Deck including the Wine and Proton compatibility layers, activated by the developer.

sources.title: Epic developer docs — anti-cheat interfaces
sources.claim: Epic's developer docs require EOS SDK 1.14 or greater and an activated Linux client module; players on Wine or Proton use the Linux client module.

sources.title: Phoronix — BattlEye works with Proton / Steam Deck
sources.claim: BattlEye works with Valve to enable Linux/Proton compatibility on the same developer opt-in model as Easy Anti-Cheat.

sources.title: Lutris
sources.claim: Lutris is a game preservation platform covering Steam, Epic Games Store, GOG and Humble Bundle plus emulator and Wine runners.

sources.title: Bottles
sources.claim: Bottles is a general-purpose Wine prefix manager for running Windows software on Linux, not an Epic library client.

sources.title: legendary-gl/legendary
sources.claim: Legendary is the free CLI/library alternative to the Epic Games Launcher and is the Epic backend Heroic wraps.

sources.title: Phoronix — Arch Linux NVIDIA open modules by default
sources.claim: Arch Linux's main NVIDIA driver packages now build the open kernel modules by default.

sources.title: Phoronix — NVIDIA R595 Linux review
sources.claim: The R595 branch brings Vulkan improvements, HDR enhancements and DRI3 v1.2 over 590.

sources.title: Phoronix — NVIDIA 590.44.01 Linux beta
sources.claim: NVIDIA raised the minimum supported Wayland version to 1.20 and improved Vulkan swapchain re-creation performance.

sources.title: NVIDIA README — PRIME render offload
sources.claim: PRIME render offload runs a chosen application on the NVIDIA dGPU while the iGPU drives the screen; Vulkan needs __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 and OpenGL also __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia.

sources.title: Phoronix — NVIDIA dynamic MUX switching proposal
sources.claim: NVIDIA proposed a new DRM-KMS-based user-space API for dynamic MUX switching because vga-switcheroo cannot express Advanced Optimus.

sources.title: Notebookcheck — Advanced Optimus support on Linux
sources.claim: Advanced Optimus / automatic MUX switching does not exist on Linux; vga-switcheroo is not built for it.

sources.title: Linuxiac — Plasma 6.8 triple buffering for NVIDIA
sources.claim: KDE Plasma 6.8 re-enables triple buffering by default for NVIDIA GPUs, reducing visible stutter.

sources.title: jp7677/dxvk-nvapi
sources.claim: DXVK-NVAPI is the NVAPI translation layer Proton ships; DLSS needs Turing-or-newer and nvngx.dll present in the prefix's system32.

sources.title: Phoronix — DXVK-NVAPI 0.9.2
sources.claim: DXVK-NVAPI 0.9.2 adds limited/incomplete Dynamic Multi-Frame Generation support and picks up the new R595 DLSS driver settings.

sources.title: ValveSoftware/gamescope
sources.claim: Gamescope is Valve's nested micro-compositor, used on desktop Linux to give a single game its own HDR, VRR and frame-limiting.

sources.title: obsproject/obs-studio
sources.claim: OBS Studio covers the streaming/manual-capture half of ShadowPlay on Linux, with NVENC encoding and a replay buffer.
